knowledge:
- key_parameters: method=In normalize(), specifies the normalization method; "mean" (default) divides each gate value by the mean of all values for that gate, while "first" divides by the first value of that gate to track changes from explicit starting conditions ;; digits=In normalize(), the number of decimal places to round and display ;; to=In cybar_plot(), sets the upper limit of the color key range to balance the color histogram ;; labels=In cybar_plot(), sets the orientation of boxplot labels (e.g., "vert" for vertical) ;; order=In cybar_plot(), if set to "sim", orders the boxplots according to the similarity calculated in the barcode heatmap ;; Rowv=In cybar_plot() and correlation(), a logical indicating whether to cluster and reorder rows ;; dendrogram=In cybar_plot() and correlation(), controls which dendrograms are plotted ("both", "row", "column", or "none") ;; abiotic=In nmds(), a data frame of environmental parameters or gate information to project onto the NMDS plot ;; p.max=In nmds(), the maximum p-value threshold for plotting abiotic/gate vectors (default is 0.05) ;; colkey=In correlation(), specifies the color palette for the correlation heatmap (e.g., heat.colors, topo.colors, cm.colors)
- alternatives: The documentation does not mention alternative packages, but notes that standard R functions like write.table are used to export results.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing flow cytometry datasets where cell abundances are recorded across gates for multiple samples (e.g., time-series or multi-treatment studies), especially when parallel environmental/abiotic data are available to correlate with population dynamics.
- pitfalls: The analysis requires highly calibrated cytometric datasets (e.g., using fluorescent beads), as any instrument shift will distort results. Missing values (NAs) are allowed in general but will cause errors in NMDS plots. If the data range (the "to" parameter) in cybar_plot is set incorrectly, the barcode color key will not be well-balanced, rendering the visualization uninformative. Using raw percental cell numbers in NMDS can distort the plot due to high/low abundance gate differences; normalized values should be preferred.

workflows.name: cybar_visualization
workflows.intent: Normalize cytometric cell abundance data and visualize community dynamics using barcodes and boxplots.
input: Cell_number_sample.txt (tab-separated text file containing sample names in the first column and cell numbers or percentages per gate in subsequent columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Read cell abundance data ;; 2. Normalize cell numbers using the "mean" or "first" method ;; 3. Convert normalized data to a data frame ;; 4. Generate cytometric barcodes and boxplots ;; 5. Save normalized values to a text file
workflows.code:
Cell_number_sample<-read.table("Cell_number_sample.txt",header=TRUE,sep="\t")  
normalize(Cell_number_sample[,-1],digits=2) 
normalize(Cell_number_sample[,-1],method="first",digits=2) 
normalized<-normalize(Cell_number_sample[,-1],digits=2) 
write.table(normalized,file="normalized.txt",row.names=TRUE,
quote=FALSE,sep="\t")
Normalized_mean<-normalize(Cell_number_sample[,-1],digits=2)
Normalized_mean<-data.frame(data.matrix(Normalized_mean))
cybar_plot(Normalized_mean,Cell_number_sample[,-1]) 
Normalized_first<-normalize(Cell_number_sample[,-1],method="first",digits=2)
Normalized_first<-data.frame(data.matrix(Normalized_first))
cybar_plot(Normalized_first,Cell_number_sample[,-1]) 
cybar_plot(x=Normalized_first,to=3.5)
cybar_plot(Normalized_mean,Cell_number_sample[,-1],labels="vert",order="sim")
cybar_plot(Normalized_first,Cell_number_sample[,-1],to=3.5,labels="vert",order="sim")
cybar_plot(x=Normalized_mean,Rowv=TRUE,grad=15,dendrogram="both",
barmain="Normalized cell numbers")
rownames(Normalized_mean)<-Cell_number_sample[,1]
cybar_plot(Normalized_mean,Cell_number_sample[,-1],
barmain="Normalized cell numbers",labels="vert",order="sim",boxmain="Cell numbers")
<<<ENDWORKFLOW

workflows.name: nmds_analysis
workflows.intent: Visualize sample dissimilarity using Nonmetric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS) and project environmental or gate variables.
input: Abiotic_data_sample.txt (tab-separated text file containing sample names, normalized gate values, and abiotic parameters)
workflows.stages: 1. Read and normalize cell abundance data ;; 2. Define sample group assignments ;; 3. Read abiotic/environmental parameter data ;; 4. Perform NMDS and plot samples, optionally overlaying groups and significant abiotic/gate vectors
workflows.code:
Normalized_mean<-normalize(Cell_number_sample[,-1],digits=2)
Normalized_mean<-data.frame(data.matrix(Normalized_mean))
nmds(Cell_number_sample[,-1])
nmds(Normalized_mean)
nmds(Normalized_mean,main="NMDS plot of 
normalized cell numbers",type="b",pos=3,pch=2,col="red")
groups<-data.frame("groups"=c(1,1,1,1,2,3,3,3,3,3))
nmds(Normalized_mean,group=groups,main="NMDS plot of 
normalized cell numbers")
data(Abiotic_data_sample)
nmds(Normalized_mean,group=groups,main="NMDS plot of 
normalized cell numbers",abiotic=Abiotic_data_sample[,-1],verbose=TRUE)
nmds(Normalized_mean,group=groups,main="NMDS plot of 
normalized cell numbers",abiotic=Abiotic_data_sample[,32:ncol(Abiotic_data_sample)],
verbose=TRUE)
nmds(Normalized_mean,group=groups,main="NMDS plot of 
normalized cell numbers",abiotic=Abiotic_data_sample[,2:31],verbose=TRUE)
nmds(Normalized_mean,group=groups,main="NMDS plot of 
normalized cell numbers",legend_pos="topright",abiotic=Abiotic_data_sample[,-1],
p.max=0.01,col_abiotic="darkred",verbose=TRUE)
rownames(Normalized_mean)<-Abiotic_data_sample[,1]
nmds(Normalized_mean,group=groups,main="NMDS plot of 
normalized cell numbers",legend_pos="topright",abiotic=Abiotic_data_sample[,-1],
p.max=0.01,col_abiotic="darkred",verbose=TRUE)
<<<ENDWORKFLOW

workflows.name: correlation_analysis
workflows.intent: Calculate and visualize Spearman's rank-order correlations between cell abundances and abiotic parameters.
input: Corr_data_sample.txt (tab-separated text file containing sample names, gate cell numbers, and abiotic parameters)
workflows.stages: 1. Read correlation dataset ;; 2. Run correlation analysis and plot heatmaps ;; 3. Customize heatmap colors, dendrograms, and column selections ;; 4. Extract and save correlation estimates and p-values
workflows.code:
data(Corr_data_sample)
correlation(Corr_data_sample[,-1])
correlation(Corr_data_sample[,-1],colkey=topo.colors(16),dendrogram="column")
correlation(Corr_data_sample[,-1],colkey=cm.colors(15),dendrogram="row")
correlation(Corr_data_sample[,-1],colkey=heat.colors(11),dendrogram="none",
main="Correlation of Corr_data_sample")
correlation(Corr_data_sample[,-1],Rowv=FALSE,Colv=FALSE,dendrogram="none")
correlation(Corr_data_sample[,c(2:11,32:34,42:ncol(Corr_data_sample))])
correlation(Corr_data_sample[,c("G1","G2","G3","G4","G5","G6","G7",
"G8","G9","G10","delta_B1","delta_B2","delta_B3","pO2","pH","redox_pot")])
cor<-correlation(Corr_data_sample[,-1],verbose=TRUE)
cor["est"]
cor["pvals"]
write.table(cor["est"],file="estimates.txt",row.names=TRUE,
quote=FALSE,sep="\t")
<<<ENDWORKFLOW
